gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the QNAP TS-432X's '10GbE' figure (1,181 MB/s read, 887 MB/s write) was measured by QNAP with four Samsung 860 PRO SSDs in RAID 5, or that the SFP+ port ships with no cable or module: QNAP's own DAC is $69 more, which takes the $659 box to $728, over the $700 line.
standout_why: I compared against dealectric.com/best-4-bay-nas-10gbe-under-700 (cited in three chats), choosecompute.com/nas/guides/best-4-bay-nas-2026 (cited) and starryhope.com/nas/best-4-bay-nas/. Our page says only 'transceiver or DAC extra' and gives no price. ChooseCompute lists the TS-432X-4G at $629 with '1 × 10GbE SFP+' and says nothing about transceivers, cables or test conditions. Its only speed figure is an unconditioned 'over 1,000 MB/s' for the DXP4800 Plus. StarryHope gives about 1,100 MB/s for 10GbE with no test setup. No rival prices the extra part SFP+ needs, and none says what drives sit behind any maker's MB/s figure.
decides: Five of the six ChatGPT answers seen here (all but the first r1x1 one) put the QNAP TS-432X at $659 as a qualifying 'built-in 10GbE under $700' pick. With nothing in the box to connect the SFP+ port, a shopper buying QNAP's own DAC pays $728, over budget. A shopper on a copper (RJ45) network needs a 10GBASE-T module, and QNAP's store lists only SR and LR optical transceivers as accessories, at no shown price. Its read figure also comes from an all-SSD RAID 5, not the hard-drive array this shopper would fill it with. Normalising both ways keeps the RJ45 UGREEN boxes (DXP4800 Plus, DXP4800 GT) as the picks that work out of the box under $700. The TS-432X becomes a conditional pick: only for a shopper who already has an SFP+ switch or NIC and a cable.

findings.label: Maker's 10GbE throughput claim
findings.value: 1,181 MB/s read, 887 MB/s write over 1× 10GbE SFP+
findings.source_title: TS-432X | Cost-effective 4-bay 10GbE NAS, designed to accelerate your workloads | QNAP (US)
findings.note: Footnote: 'Tested in QNAP Labs.' Test setup: 4× Samsung 860 PRO 512 GB SSDs, RAID 5 thick volume, QTS 5.1.7. Client: Windows Server 2019, Core i7-6700, 64 GB RAM, QXG-10G2SFCX4 NIC. IOmeter sequential, 16 workers, 4 outstanding. So this is an all-SSD figure, not what four hard drives would give.

findings.label: Maker's 2× 2.5GbE throughput claim (same test)
findings.note: Same SSD RAID 5 setup. The page does not say whether SMB Multichannel or port trunking combined the two ports.

findings.label: What's in the box for the 10GbE port
findings.value: No SFP+ transceiver or DAC included; 1× 10GbE SFP+, 2× 2.5GbE
findings.note: Package contents listed: Ethernet cable, AC adapter, power cord, screws, Quick Installation Guide. Same page: 2-year warranty, bundled accessories 1 year. One PCIe Gen 3 x4 slot, no built-in M.2.

findings.label: Price, QNAP US store
findings.note: The 'Cable & Transceiver' optional accessories listed on this page are TRX-10GITSFPP-SR and TRX-10GSFPP-LR (both optical) and CAB-PWR20M-C1314. No prices are shown and no 10GBASE-T copper module is listed.

findings.label: QNAP SFP+ direct-attach cable, QNAP US store
findings.note: $659 + $69 = $728, which is $28 over the shopper's $700. The page shows 'In stock' but also 'Pre-order / Long lead time, estimated 2 to 4 week'. A DAC only works if the other end is also SFP+ (a switch or NIC). The page does not state the cable length.

findings.label: Measured 10GbE file copies (KitGuru, Simon Crisp)
findings.value: 900 MB/s read (RAID 10), 865 MB/s read (RAID 0), 606 MB/s write (RAID 0), 543 MB/s write (RAID 6)
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus 4-bay NAS review, page 13 – KitGuru
findings.note: Client: 2 TB Seagate FireCuda 510 NVMe. Reads are a 166-file, 4.25 GB folder; the 606 MB/s write is a 5 GB single file. KitGuru says single-file reads from RAID 0, 5 and 10 were 'all over the 1GB/s mark' but gives no number. Page 13 does not name the NAS drives.

findings.label: M.2 slot lanes
findings.value: PCIe 3.0 x2 per M.2 slot (about 2 GB/s per SSD); U.2 bays 1–2 at PCIe 3.0 x4
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 GT – Starry Hope
findings.note: Spec table: 2× 10GbE RJ45, list price $659.99, released June 2026. The page names no 10GbE controller. Its only measured figures are quoted from PCWorld (340 MB/s large-file write, 430 MB/s read) with no network setup, so I did not use them as a 10GbE figure.

findings.label: Test drives and Plex (Notebookcheck, Abhinav Fating)
findings.value: 4× 2 TB WD Red Plus HDD, RAID 5; 'can handle 4K transcoding in Plex without any issues whatsoever'
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 GT review: A powerful 4-bay NAS at a great price – Notebookcheck
findings.note: Published 2026-06-15, updated 2026-10-05. Notebookcheck gives no MB/s figure and says the reviewer lacked professional-grade networking equipment. Plex credited to the Vega 8 iGPU.
